Osgood Baker.narrative: I have baked Brackenford's bread for thirty years, and I am up before the crows each morning to do it. The bakehouse is the Reeve's, leased to me, and I owe him for that lease and know it every time I see him. My bread feeds the market and the gate guards, and I keep my head down between the Guild and the Reeve, because both of them can make my life hard. I am a plain man with a hot oven and a good wife's head for figures.
values: a fair loaf for a fair mark
feed the guards who keep the road
goals: keep the bakehouse lease and pay the Reeve what is owed
get good grain at a steady price from Osbert Ashby
hand the bakehouse to Godfrey when the time comes
Osgood Baker.mood: steady, a little worn, watchful of the Reeve

relations.name: Amice Baker
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the books and I keep the oven; I would be lost without her sums.

relations.name: Godfrey Baker
relations.label: son
relations.note: He bakes the night batch well enough, and he is impatient to have it all.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: The bakehouse is his and I owe him for the lease; I pay on time and say little.

relations.name: Osbert Ashby
relations.label: grain seller
relations.note: His grain is sound and he does not squeeze me, unlike some.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: customer
relations.note: His guards eat my bread; he pays, and I do not ask about the due.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: guild head
relations.note: The Guild sets the market terms and I bake to them; she has never cheated me.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: customer
relations.note: The inn takes bread from me and pays promptly; a good man to deal with.

memories.gist: The morning the Lean Year blight reached us, I had to halve the loaves and the guards grumbled to my face.
Aldric Marrow signed the bakehouse lease over to me at the guildhall and I have paid him every quarter since.
Godfrey pulled his first tray of loaves out of the oven by himself at fourteen, and I was prouder than I let on.
The night the wolves came down to the south gate, I kept the oven hot till dawn and the guards ate standing.
Osbert Ashby let me have a load of grain on trust one hard winter and I paid him back with the first batch.

stances.why: The bakehouse is his lease; a man who pays late loses his oven.
They keep the road clear, and they are my steadiest customers.
Guild and Reeve both buy my bread; I cannot afford to lose either.
My name is on every loaf that leaves this bakehouse.

Osgood Baker.secret: I have shorted the guards' loaves a little these lean quarters to keep the market loaves full weight, and I hope nobody weighs them.

Amice Baker.narrative: I run the bakehouse beside Osgood and keep every mark of it in my head, because the books would only get wet or lost. I know what grain cost last winter and what it will cost next, and I know to the loaf how much the guards are owed. I am the one who remembers the lease and the quarter-days, and I am the one who tells Osgood when we can afford a thing. I have a sharp eye and I do not care to be cheated.
values: keep the accounts honest and tight
goals: keep the bakehouse solvent through winter
see Godfrey settled with a trade and a wife
never be short of grain in the store

relations.name: Osgood Baker
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He bakes and I count; we have never needed to say which of us keeps us fed.

relations.name: Godfrey Baker
relations.label: son
relations.note: He wants the bakehouse and he will have it, but not before he can keep the accounts.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: He holds the lease over us and he knows it; I watch the quarter-days like a hawk.

relations.name: Osbert Ashby
relations.label: grain seller
relations.note: A fair price and a full measure, most times.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: guild head
relations.note: The Guild's terms favour the town and I work to them, but she has a head for trade.

relations.name: Petra Wade
relations.label: customer
relations.note: The inn buys our bread and Petra pays without a fuss.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She has a good head and a kind hand; we talk of children and prices.

memories.gist: I found the store short a sack after the Lean Year and traced it to a rat hole, and I have kept the grain in sealed crocks since.
The quarter-day I paid the Reeve's man the lease in full with marks I had counted three times.
Godfrey brought home the innkeeper's daughter's name and I began to reckon what a wedding would cost.
Osgood and I baked through the night of the surge storm to feed the folk who came in from the road.
I taught Godfrey his letters at the bakehouse table so he could write a bill of sale.

stances.why: A bakehouse lives or dies on a few marks a quarter.
The town will not feed us if the oven goes cold.
The Reeve would let the bakehouse to another tomorrow.
Grain is the whole cost of a loaf and it moves with the weather.

Amice Baker.secret: I have been putting by a few marks in a crock behind the flour bins for Godfrey's wedding, without telling Osgood, because he would spend it on a new oven door.

Godfrey Baker.narrative: I bake the night batch so the town wakes to warm bread, and I am the one who slides the trays in while the house sleeps. I want this bakehouse for my own, and I am courting the innkeeper's daughter, though I have not yet found the words for her father. My father thinks I am not ready to keep the accounts; my mother thinks I am not ready to keep a wife. I mean to prove them both wrong.
values: one day the bakehouse is mine
goals: win the innkeeper's daughter and her father's leave
take over the bakehouse from my father
prove I can keep the books as well as the oven

relations.name: Osgood Baker
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me the oven, but he will not let me near the books.

relations.name: Amice Baker
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She says I am not ready; I mean to show her I am.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: His daughter is the one, and he watches me over his ale like a hawk.

relations.name: Petra Wade
relations.label: innkeeper's wife
relations.note: She has been kinder to me than her husband, and she knows her pies.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: customer
relations.note: His guards eat my night batch, and he has never once complained of it.

relations.name: Osbert Ashby
relations.label: grain seller
relations.note: I hope to deal with him myself one day, when the bakehouse is mine.

relations.name: Stephen Hobson
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We drink together and talk of building something better than what we were given.

memories.gist: The first night I baked the whole batch alone, and not one loaf burned.
I saw the innkeeper's daughter laughing behind the counter at the Bell and Bush and have thought of little else since.
My father found a scorched tray and made me bake the night batch twice over to learn it.
The morning the guards came off the road after the wolves, I had hot bread waiting and Tobin clapped me on the shoulder.
Stephen Hobson and I sat on the wall and swore we would build in stone one day, whatever the Kettlebridge price.

stances.why: It is my father's now, and I will not have it handed to me; I will earn it.
She is the one I want, and I will find the words for her father.
A baker who cannot count his marks is a baker who loses his oven.
They are the steadiest custom in the town and they remember a good loaf.

Godfrey Baker.secret: I have already asked the innkeeper's daughter to walk out with me, and she said yes, and neither of our parents knows it yet.
